title: Excise harness summary v1
description: The result of one validation harness run. Internal test tooling, not a supported product interface.

run_id.description: Also the name of the run's output directory.

latency_budget_scale.description: The factor the latency budgets (input_to_frame_p99_ms, max_stall_ms, first_frame_ms, quit_ms) of the scenarios that were expected to pass were multiplied by. Present only when it is above 1, so a strict run has no such field; no other budget is ever scaled, and a scenario expected to fail is judged against the strict budgets either way.

timing_informational.description: Present, and true, when the run held timing informational: a timing budget a result missed (a scenario's four latency budgets, a headless scan's ratio against du) is a warning in that result's timing_warnings, not a failure. Absent in a strict run. Every other budget blocked as usual, and a result that was expected to fail was judged strictly either way.

quick_tier_ms.description: How long the whole quick tier took, in milliseconds, from just before the first launch of the binary under test to the end of the last run: the time held to the tier's budget. Present only in a run of the whole quick tier (--quick with no --scenario, --profile, or --repeat); absent from every other run, which is not the tier, and from every headless run.

verdict.description: xpass means an expected failure passed; it fails the run.

metrics.description: Named measurements. Every value is a finite number. This is a deliberately open map: the harness does not constrain which metric names appear, since each scenario and fixture names its own (for example `peak_rss_bytes`, `idle_output_bytes`, `idle_cpu_ms`, `scan_store_peak_bytes`, `scan_store_bytes_per_entry`, `cgroup_memory_peak_bytes`, `threads`, `fds`, `residue_files`, a headless fixture's `memory_budget_bytes` and oracle-diff counts, or any scenario `measure` name). Consumers must not assume a fixed set of keys.

timing_warnings.description: The timing budgets this result missed while the run held timing informational: warnings that left the verdict as it was. Absent when there are none, and always absent from a strict run.

timing_warning.description: A timing budget a result missed and was not failed for, because the run held timing informational. The value is above the limit.

budget.description: Only a budget that the speed of the machine decides: the four latency budgets and the three ratio budgets. Every other budget fails the run when it is missed.
